## apply_patch | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/apply-patch.txt | 2150 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Use `apply_patch` for localized source edits and related multi-file changes. Put the exact patch envelope in `patchText`. Call this tool directly; never invoke `apply_patch` through `bash` or wrap it in a shell heredoc.

Selection:
- Prefer this tool over a full-file rewrite for existing hand-edited files.
- Do not use it for generated files or bulk mechanical rewrites; run the owning generator, formatter, or narrowly scoped transformation instead.
- Use `write` only for a new file best expressed as complete content or an intentional full replacement after reading the current file.
- `git apply` is a shell fallback only for an already-supplied standard unified diff whose provenance and target paths you understand. Read every affected existing file and run `git apply --check` before the real command. Freshness comes from current file bytes and patch context, not Git metadata.

Recovery:
- All sections are parsed and verified before the first filesystem change. If a hunk header or context no longer matches, read the affected file and retry with a smaller patch using fresh, unique context.
- Do not resend the same patch after a verification failure.
- If `git apply --check` or `git apply` fails, stop and re-read every affected file. Translate the smallest still-required change to native `apply_patch` or structured `edit` when exposed; do not mechanically retry the failed diff.
- Do not add `--3way` or `--reject` as automatic recovery, because they can change merge semantics or leave partial artifacts. Never use `git reset --hard` or `git checkout --` to make a patch fit.
- If the result is `uncertain`, some paths may already have changed. Inspect every reported path before retrying; never replay the patch mechanically.

Format:
- Start with `*** Begin Patch`, end with `*** End Patch`, and include one or more file sections.
- Start each section with `*** Add File: <path>`, `*** Delete File: <path>`, or `*** Update File: <path>`.
- An update may include `*** Move to: <path>` and uses `@@` hunks with context, removed (`-`), and added (`+`) lines.
- Every initial-content line in an Add File section must start with `+`.
>>>

## bash | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/bash.txt | 1321 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Executes a command with the configured shell. Commands are parsed with tree-sitter before execution so each constituent command is permission-checked independently. A deterministic destructive-command gate runs before every foreground or background spawn. Replacing an existing redirect target requires fresh human approval; creating a new static file in the OS temp directory does not. For one-off scripts, prefer interpreter stdin such as `python3 - <<'PY'` over fixed `/tmp` filenames. This is not a sandbox: commands retain the user's full filesystem, network, and credentials; confinement is a future decision, not an implied guarantee. Use workdir instead of changing directories inside the command.

For source changes, prefer native `apply_patch` or structured `edit`, which validate current file bytes or context and report a structured diff. Use `git apply` only for an already-supplied standard unified diff whose provenance and paths you understand: read every affected existing file, run `git apply --check`, and apply it only when that preflight succeeds. Git is not a stale-read or rollback authority. If the check or apply fails, stop, re-read current files, and use a smaller native patch/edit. Do not automatically add `--3way` or `--reject`; never recover with `git reset --hard` or `git checkout --`.
>>>

## goal_propose | crates/zuno-goal/src/description/create-goal.txt | 420 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Create a durable goal only when explicitly requested by the user or higher-priority instructions. Do not infer a goal from ordinary work. Preserve the requested objective without narrowing it. Record concrete success_criteria when the request defines them; they are immutable to the model after creation. An unfinished goal cannot be replaced. Set token_budget only when the user explicitly requested a positive budget.
>>>

## edit | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/edit.txt | 1411 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Applies one or more exact string replacements to a file atomically.

Usage:
- Read this exact file before editing it. Zuno tracks a content digest for the current session and rejects stale edits after an external change.
- The stale-read guard compares the exact bytes recorded by `read`; it does not depend on a Git repository, index, or status.
- Put ordered operations in `edits`. Each operation sees the result of the preceding operation; if any operation fails, nothing is written.
- When editing text from Read tool output, preserve the exact indentation after the line number prefix and never include the prefix in oldString or newString.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit fails if oldString is absent or non-unique unless replaceAll is true.
- Use replaceAll for replacing and renaming strings across the file.
- After a failed native patch or `git apply`, re-read the file before translating the smallest still-required change into exact edit operations. Never use `git reset --hard` or `git checkout --` to make stale text match.
Example:
{"filePath":"/workspace/src/lib.rs","edits":[
  {"oldString":"fn old_name()","newString":"fn new_name()"},
  {"oldString":"old_name()","newString":"new_name()","replaceAll":true}
]}
>>>

## glob | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/glob.txt | 516 bytes | trailing-newline: no
<<<
- Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size
- Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts"
- Returns matching file paths
- Use this tool when you need to find files by name patterns
- When you are doing an open-ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Task tool instead
- You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. It is always better to speculatively perform multiple searches as a batch that are potentially useful.
>>>

## grep | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/grep.txt | 656 bytes | trailing-newline: no
<<<
- Fast content search tool that works with any codebase size
- Searches file contents using regular expressions
- Supports full regex syntax (eg. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+", etc.)
- Filter files by pattern with the include parameter (eg. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}")
- Returns file paths and line numbers with matching lines
- Use this tool when you need to find files containing specific patterns
- If you need to identify/count the number of matches within files, use the Bash tool with `rg` (ripgrep) directly. Do NOT use `grep`.
- When you are doing an open-ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Task tool instead
>>>

## memory_propose | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/memory-propose.txt | 432 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Propose one durable resident-memory change for user review. Use global only for cross-project preferences and project for repository-specific rules. Record stable facts, user corrections, or verified reusable recovery knowledge. Never record secrets, temporary environment failures, unresolved guesses, task progress, or one-off narratives. This tool creates an auditable candidate; it does not imply the resident file was changed.

## plan_exit | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/plan-exit.txt | 812 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Use this tool when you have completed the planning phase and are ready to exit plan agent.

This tool asks the user whether to switch to the orchestrator and start implementing the plan.

Call this tool:
- After you have written a complete plan to the plan file
- After every material question is resolved and no unresolved implementation decision remains
- When another agent can execute the plan without repeating discovery

Do NOT call this tool:
- Before you have created or finalized the plan
- If you still have unanswered questions about the implementation
- If the user has indicated they want to continue planning
- Merely because you have reached the end of a turn

Do not duplicate the approval question in chat; this tool owns that interaction. A cancellation or "No" keeps the session in plan mode.
>>>

## question | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/question.txt | 948 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Use this tool when you need to ask the user questions during execution. This allows you to:
1. Gather user preferences or requirements
2. Clarify ambiguous instructions
3. Get decisions on implementation choices as you work
4. Offer choices to the user about what direction to take.

Usage notes:
- Ask only when the answer materially changes the outcome and cannot be discovered from available evidence
- Prefer one concise question and ask no more than three at once
- When `custom` is enabled (default), a "Type your own answer" option is added automatically; don't include "Other" or catch-all options
- Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive options; set `multiple: true` only when combinations are meaningful
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label
- Answers are returned as arrays of labels
- Cancellation is a refusal, not an answer; do not fabricate a selection
>>>

## read | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/read.txt | 1083 bytes | trailing-newline: no
<<<
Read a file or directory from the local filesystem. If the path does not exist, an error is returned.

Usage:
- The filePath parameter should be an absolute path.
- By default, this tool returns up to 2000 lines from the start of the file.
- The offset parameter is the line number to start from (1-indexed).
- To read later sections, call this tool again with a larger offset.
- Use the grep tool to find specific content in large files or files with long lines.
- If you are unsure of the correct file path, use the glob tool to look up filenames by glob pattern.
- Contents are returned with each line prefixed by its line number as `<line>: <content>`. For directories, entries are returned one per line (without line numbers) with a trailing `/` for subdirectories.
- Any line longer than 2000 characters is truncated.
- Call this tool in parallel when you know there are multiple files you want to read.
- Avoid tiny repeated slices (30 line chunks). If you need more context, read a larger window.
- This tool can read image files and PDFs and return them as file attachments.
>>>

## skill | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/skill.txt | 724 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Discover and read reusable skill instructions through progressive disclosure.
Use action `list` to page through all model-visible skills, or action `search` with a concise task intent; optional search `limit` is 1-20. Metadata results include the exact `source` needed to distinguish same-named skills.
Use action `load` with the selected `name` and `source`. Follow `next_cursor` until `complete` before acting; a partial SKILL.md is not usable guidance.
Use action `read_resource` with the same `name` and `source`, a relative `path` such as `references/ci.md`, and any returned continuation cursor. Do not use shell, find, glob, or broad filesystem scans to rediscover an advertised skill or locate its referenced files.
>>>

## task | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/task.txt | 1079 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Delegate a self-contained unit of work to a subagent in its own session.
Name exactly one of `subagent_type` (a specific Agent) or `category` (a preset shorthand, which runs the `general` Agent at that preset's model).
State the goal, success evidence, relevant files or sources, constraints, and explicit in/out-of-scope boundaries. The parent retains integration decisions and final verification.
Foreground is the default and blocks until the child answers; `background: true` returns immediately with a fresh job id.
Background jobs default to `reportDelivery: "nextStep"`, which adds the terminal report to the parent's next step and wakes it. Use `"quiet"` only when the persisted job result will be inspected separately.
Pass `task_id` from a previous call to continue that same child session instead of starting a fresh one.
Skills are not an argument: each agent's permissions already decide which skills it can load.
Do not delegate work you are simultaneously performing yourself, and do not create overlapping children unless their ownership boundaries are explicit.
>>>

## plan_get | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/plan-get.txt | 263 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Read the durable plan for the current session.
Returns null when no plan exists. Read it before plan_update so the update can carry the current revision and preserve stable step ids.
This tool is read-only and safe to call in parallel with other read-only tools.
>>>

## plan_update | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/plan-update.txt | 541 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Create or update the durable plan for the current session.
When a plan already exists, expected_revision is required and must equal the revision returned by plan_get. A stale revision is rejected without changing the plan.
Keep every step id stable across updates. Step ids and titles must be non-empty and unique.
Link the plan to the active goal with goal_id when one exists. Do not rewrite the user's goal or success criteria through this tool.
This tool changes durable state and is never replayed implicitly after an uncertain failure.
>>>

## todo_get | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/todo-get.txt | 289 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Read durable work items for the current session.
Returns stable ids, revisions, goal and plan links, parent and dependency ids, owner, status, priority, timing, and token usage.
Read the current items before todo_update so every update or removal can carry the matching expected_revision.
>>>

## todo_update | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/todo-update.txt | 797 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Atomically add, update, or remove durable work items for the current session.
Pass changes as objects tagged with action: add, update, or remove. Updates and removals require the stable id and expected_revision returned by todo_get.
An add may omit id to let Zuno create one. Preserve an existing id instead of deleting and recreating an item.
Every referenced parent, dependency, and plan_step_id must exist after the batch. Parent and dependency graphs must be acyclic.
At most one item may be in_progress in a session. Use active_form for the short present-tense activity shown while that item runs.
The whole batch rolls back on any validation or revision error; partial updates are never committed.
This tool changes durable state and is never replayed implicitly after an uncertain failure.
>>>

## goal_update | crates/zuno-goal/src/description/update-goal.txt | 591 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Read the current goal before changing it and pass its revision as expected_revision. If the revision is stale, read again instead of overwriting concurrent work. Mark it complete only when authoritative evidence proves every requirement and no required work remains. Report blocked only with a concrete blocking_condition after the same true impasse persists for three consecutive goal turns and meaningful progress is impossible without user input or external change. Do not use this tool merely because a turn is ending, work is difficult, the budget is low, or more verification remains.
>>>

## webfetch | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/webfetch.txt | 749 bytes | trailing-newline: no
<<<
- Fetches content from a specified URL
- Takes a URL and optional format as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts to requested format (markdown by default)
- Returns the content in the specified format
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: if another tool is present that offers better web fetching capabilities, is more targeted to the task, or has fewer restrictions, prefer using that tool instead of this one.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - Format options: "markdown" (default), "text", or "html"
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large
>>>

## write | crates/zuno-tools/src/description/write.txt | 1158 bytes | trailing-newline: yes
<<<
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- Only `filePath` and `content` are required.
- If this is an existing file, read that exact file first. Zuno tracks its content digest for the current session and rejects stale writes after an external change.
- The stale-read guard compares the exact bytes recorded by `read`; it does not depend on a Git repository, index, or status.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.
- Do not use a full-file write as a blind fallback after native patch or `git apply` failure; re-read first and replace the whole file only when that replacement is intentional. Never use `git reset --hard` or `git checkout --` to manufacture the expected pre-image.
Example: {"filePath":"/workspace/new.txt","content":"complete file contents\n"}
>>>
